headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0072 — SMTO can't tell if your OneDrive or SharePoint change worked

html:
SMTO-SKL-0072 — SMTO can't tell if your OneDrive or SharePoint change worked

GUID: 6f1178e4-b639-588b-8efc-e607c6979c11
Slug: microsoft365-file-mutation-outcome-unknown
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • SMTO sent your file change to Microsoft, but the reply was lost or incomplete. The upload, move, copy, new folder or delete may or may not have happened, so SMTO won't repeat it on its own.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened: open OneDrive or the SharePoint library in your browser with the same Microsoft account and look in the folder SMTO was working in. Microsoft may have finished the change even though SMTO never got the reply.
  2. For an upload or copy, look for the file by name; for a move, check both folders; for a delete, check that folder and the recycle bin. Each kind of change leaves a different sign that it went through.
  3. Only if the change is clearly missing, ask SMTO to do it again and approve it when asked. Repeating a change that already happened could leave a duplicate file or move the wrong item.

What success looks like

  • The folder in OneDrive or SharePoint shows the file or change exactly once, as you intended.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file name and time, to the person who manages SMTO's Microsoft 365 setup. Don't keep repeating the upload or copy; each repeat could create another copy.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Microsoft 365 file mutation (upload, folder create, move, delete or copy) lost a reliable result: the connection failed or returned a server error after the write was sent, the final upload chunk returned no item ID, or an asynchronous copy returned no monitor Location.

What this means

  • File mutation loses a reliable result, final upload lacks an item ID, or asynchronous copy lacks its required monitor Location. Microsoft may already have applied the mutation. A lost or unverifiable result is not proof of nonexecution; inspect exact resource and correlation evidence before another write.

Why this can happen

  • File mutation loses a reliable result, final upload lacks an item ID, or asynchronous copy lacks its required monitor Location.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact destination, upload session, item ID and copy monitor evidence.

How to fix it

  • Check whether your action already happened: read the destination with microsoft365.file_list or file_info under the same account_ref (for uploads, the result's uploaded_bytes_confirmed shows the last confirmed offset). Only if the item is absent or unchanged, issue a new deliberate request; never replay the original mutation or start a replacement transfer before the outcome is known.
  • Inspect the exact destination file and upload/copy correlation; do not start a replacement transfer until the previous outcome is reconciled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The remote file outcome is reconciled before another file mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • Microsoft may already have applied the mutation. A lost or unverifiable result is not proof of nonexecution; inspect exact resource and correlation evidence before another write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
